newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Liberal win at the Lindsay by-election means a re-endorsement of the Howard Government's electoral mandate and will see the Senate under pressure to pass key elements of the Government's economic agenda. Prime Minister John Howard classed Jackie Kelly's win in Lindsay as a "defining event." Page 1.

The Federal Government and the Democrats are likely to agree on non-union employment contracts being vetted by an independent "umpire" as part of a compromise to allow the industrial relations reforms to pass through the Senate. Page 1.

The High Court ruling in the Victoria and others v the Commonwealth case, which saw the quashing of laws against "harsh, unjust and unreasonable" dismissal, has had a strong impact in the Industrial Relations Court, with several judges moving to shore up workers' unfair dismissal protection. Page 3.

Liberal candidate in the Lindsay by-election, Jackie Kelly, was not affected by the financially strong efforts of the Shooters Party and the Australians Against Further Immigration, which both fell far short of pre-poll expectations. Voters seemed more concerned with giving Kelly a fair go, than worrying about gun control or Budget measures. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Prime Minister John Howard has warned critics to "get out of my way" after the Liberal Party secured victory in the Lindsay by-election. Speaking to delegates at the Liberal Party Federal Council meeting in Hobart, Howard said the victory would see those opposed to his party's reforms face an electoral backlash unless they "let the new crowd have a fair go". Page 1.

Both Australian Labor Party national secretary Gary Gray and Liberal Party Federal director Andrew Robb have indicated Queensland Independent MP Pauline Hanson's chances of retaining her seat in Federal Parliament were slim, with both major parties denying her preferences in the next election. Page 1.

World motorcycle champion Michael Doohan has blamed his Honda team mate Alex Criville for a crash on the ninth turn of the final lap that cost Doohan a probable third victory in the Australian 500cc motorcycle grand prix in Sydney yesterday. Page 1.

The Australian Medical Association will back a decision by young doctors to hold a national day of industrial action to force Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge to negotiate over his plans to reduce Medicare provider numbers for trainee doctors. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Prime Minister John Howard and his Government have claimed a second mandate to continue with their legislative program, including the introduction of the Workplace Relations Bill and the partial privatisation of Telstra, after the stunning Liberal victory in the Lindsay by-election. Page 1.

Re-elected Member for Lindsay Jackie Kelly was hailed by Prime Minister John Howard as the Liberal Party's new love as she arrived at the Liberal Party Federal Council in Hobart to a standing ovation. However, Kelly kept her feet on the ground, declaring that her constituency was her first priority. Page 1.

In a major expansion of his plan to return Sydney's Government House to the people, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr has offered to open the doors and grounds of the building to cultural organisations. State Opposition Leader Peter Collins believes the mve will see Government House suffering the ultimate indignity. Page 1.

Researchers at Douglass Hanly Moir Pathology in Sydney suggest the number of women who are wrongly told their Pap smear result is clear could be reduced significantly through the use of the PAPNET system, an expensive, automated system that is used to anayse the tests. The system prevented seven to 10 women from the 54,000 tested from developing cervical cancer. Page 3.
THE AGE

National Crime Authority chairman John Broome has hit out at what he describes as a campaign within the Federal Government to abolish the NCA or severely reduce its powers. While Broome said the campaign was rapidly escalating, he believed the Authority till had the support of Cabinet, its parliamentary joint committee and State Governments in general. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard said the Liberal win in the Lindsay by-election confirmed that voters wanted a change of direction in the March Federal election. While the Liberal result showed a 6.1 per cent swing, the Labor Party suffered a loss of seven per cent, the Australians Against Further Immigration Party more than doubled its vote from 2.7 per cent to 6.1 per cent and the Democrats slumped from 4.9 per cent to 1.6 per cent. Page 1.

Victorian Conservation Minister Marie Tehan is on the defensive following conflict-of-interest allegations over her shareholding in a company that is part of the consortium awarded the contract to introduce automated ticketing on Melbourne's public transprt system. Page 1.

Family Court judge Justice John Fogarty claims inappropriately removing young people with behaviour problems from residential units and placing them in foster care has led to a number of tragedies. Fogarty said placement decisions taken by State Government departments were often dictated by policy and funding rather than the welfare of children in State care. Page 2.
